title: A research wiki on neurotechnology and justice
problem: Our team keeps losing track of what each report says about neurotechnology in the justice system. Build us a research wiki we can trust and keep up to date.
facilitator_brief: The wiki is already compiled from nine sources (WORKSHOP_DATA.wiki), following Karpathy's LLM-wiki pattern as kept in a book project: source, concept, entity and question pages, verified pins that open the PDF page, registers and contested claims. The app is the team's workspace for it: read and navigate, Ask the wiki and file good answers back, Ingest the waiting source A/HRC/57/61 with a human approving each change, and Lint. The model drafts; the code verifies every quotation.
notes:
The problem as I read it: a team reads the same ten documents on neurotechnology in the justice system and keeps losing what each one says. The facilitator's brief turns that into a division of labour that already exists in the data: a wiki written by models from nine documents, where the model drafts and files, the code checks every quotation against the library, and a person approves each change. The app is the workspace around that wiki, so I began with the wiki itself.

 The wiki: 40 pages, each with `slug`, `type`, `title`, `frontmatter` and `body`, and four markdown documents at the top level: the schema (1,972 words), the index (1,065 words), the log (738) and the tensions register (721).  The library: ten documents. `symbol` is filled for 5 of 10 (the NHRI report, the submission and the two articles have none) and `paragraph` is set only in the UN reports and the General Comments, so a citation reads "para. 41" for half the library and "p. 3471" or "p. e773" for the rest. `status` is "ingested" for nine and "inbox" for A/HRC/57/61.

 A source page (AHRC 2025): full cite, register with a warning never to cite it as (b), a one-liner, key takeaways with a pin on every sentence, 28 links in the frontmatter.  A concept page (self-incrimination) walks the registers from the top: (a) treaty text with a plain link, because the ICCPR is not in the library, then (b), (c) and down.  An entity page (the UNESCO Recommendation) follows one thing through four documents by date, and already links to [[a-hrc-57-61]]: the inbox document has a page. It is an entity stub, `status` "stub", with 11 pins all to other documents and a list of ten things the ingest should check. 16 pages link to it.

 The contested blocks: six, each on a concept page, with `claim:`, `verdict:`, `note:` and position lines (sign, register, pin, gloss, page); the verdicts are three leans-contest, two contested, one leans-support.  Pins: 707, exactly the index's number, all marked ✓. I then ran the schema's verification rule in a script of my own. 625 quotes sit whole in one passage of the named PDF page; 82 contain "…" and join fragments of one passage, so a plain substring check would fail 82 of 707. With the fragments matched in order inside one passage, capitals kept, curly quotes straightened, dashes made hyphens and a hyphen followed by a space removed, all 707 verify, and every label's "para." or "p." matches a passage on that page. Pins per document run from 227 (A/81/351) to 17 (Prainsack); none to A/HRC/57/61.  The inbox document: 100 passages on PDF pages 2 to 20, 61,737 characters, paragraphs 1 to 84 with sub-paragraphs as separate passages ("78 (a)"); the passage labelled "5 (a)" carries (b) and (c) inside its text, and `section` is broken in two places ("risks", and a sentence fragment) where a heading crossed a page. 13 passages mention justice, courts, police or prisons; 29 once evidence, torture and the recommendations are added. The report is about all human rights; the wiki is about one setting.  A question page: short answer, reasoning with pins, what the library cannot answer, related pages.

My own counts, for the lint: no dangling link, no orphan, `sources` equals the pinned documents on every page; frontmatter `links` and body links differ on 5 entries. Bodies run from 3,980 to 23,216 characters, 347,911 in all, roughly 87,000 tokens: an Ask cannot send the wiki, so the index is the entry, as the schema says. The bodies use headings, bullets, numbered lists, plain links and pins, no tables or images, so a small renderer is enough.

On the shelf, five searches.  The LLM-wiki pattern.  The author's own schema.  Human review of AI-generated changes.  Accessible status messages and focus.  Citing UN documents, which I did not read further: the wiki's schema already fixes the citation form of every pin.  Karpathy's summary gives the frame: raw sources are never edited, the index is read first, the log is append-only, ingest one source at a time and stay involved.  The author's schema adds what the wiki already follows: the direct-link rule, ✓ and ⚠, registers never blurred, a contested block whose authored verdict leads the bar, a lint for orphans, dangling links and unverified pins.  The quality-assurance guidance on generative AI gives the two rules the app enforces: never use what a model generated without reviewing it, and treat the model's input as a public website, hence a running count of what has left the browser.  The A11Y checklist: visible focus, unique button labels, labelled inputs, a 4.5:1 contrast, captions on tables.

The trade-offs are cost and size. A `studio.ask` answer is capped at about 8,000 tokens and each call costs money. The source page needs about 900 words and the touched pages, five to fifteen by the schema, about 300 words each, so the ingest runs in steps: takeaways from the passages, then the source page, then one call per touched page, each verified by the code before a person sees it. 100 passages exceed the 25-per-call rule, hence batches; what to send is a human decision (q1), as are the grain of approval (q2), what to do with a quotation the code cannot find (q3), whether Ask also sends library passages (q4) and whether an answer separates the law from the commentary (q5). The page has no storage, so changes live in memory with a download button, and the model is never called on load.

questions.question: Which passages of the inbox document leave the browser when the model drafts its source page?

options.label: Whole report
options.description: All passages go, in batches of 25; the model sees the report as its authors wrote it, at four calls' cost for A/HRC/57/61.

fragments.text: **Scope: the whole document.** The panel says: "All `passages.length` passages will be sent, in batches of 25 (n calls), c characters; nothing is held back." A table lists the batches with their paragraph ranges and PDF pages. **Start** runs them one after another with a progress line ("batch 2 of 4 · 50 of 100 passages have left the browser") and a Stop button that keeps what has returned.
- **Batches** = the document's `passages` in file order, cut every 25; the number of calls = ceil(n ÷ 25). Every passage is sent exactly once.
- **Coverage.** Passages sent equal `passages.length`; every takeaway's `passage` id is among them; a takeaway naming a passage that was not sent is dropped and counted.

options.label: Screened passages
options.description: A keyword screen pre-ticks the passages on justice, custody, evidence and the recommendations (29 of 100 in the file I looked at); you tick or untick before sending; one or two calls.

fragments.text: **Scope: screened passages.** The code pre-ticks the passages that match the justice screen (the words are listed on screen) and the recommendations section; the panel shows "n of `passages.length` passages ticked, c characters, k calls" and a checklist grouped by PDF page where each passage can be ticked or unticked, with its paragraph number and first words. **Start** sends the ticked passages in batches of 25 with the same progress line and Stop button; the unticked ones stay listed under "not sent", so the source page cannot cite them and a reader knows why.

- **Screen** = a passage is pre-ticked when its `text` matches `/justice|court|criminal|police|prison|detain|sentenc|lie detect|offender|forensic|interrogat|evidence|self-incrimination|torture/i` or its `section` starts with "VII" (the recommendations). The ticked set, in file order, is cut every 25; the number of calls = ceil(ticked ÷ 25). Unticked passages are never sent in that run.
- **Coverage.** Passages sent equal the ticked count; the panel names how many were left out. A takeaway naming an unsent passage is dropped and counted.

options.label: Sections I tick
options.description: Nothing is pre-selected: you tick whole sections of the report (its headings, with passage counts) before anything is sent.

fragments.text: **Scope: sections you tick.** A checklist of the document's `section` headings in file order, each with its passage count and PDF pages, none ticked. A `section` that is a broken fragment (shorter than 12 characters, or not starting with a Roman numeral, a capital letter or a letter and a full stop) is shown as "continuation of the previous heading" and ticked with it. The panel shows "n passages in k sections ticked, c characters, m calls"; **Start** sends them in batches of 25 with the progress line and Stop button; the sections left out are listed under "not sent".

- **Selection** = the passages whose `section` is ticked (a continuation `section` belongs to the heading before it), in file order, cut every 25; the number of calls = ceil(selected ÷ 25). Unticked sections are never sent in that run.
- **Coverage.** Passages sent equal the ticked sections' passage counts added up; the panel names the sections left out. A takeaway naming an unsent passage is dropped and counted.

questions.question: At what grain does a person approve the changes an ingest proposes?

options.label: Per page
options.description: One decision per page touched: the new source page, then each edited page with all its inserted paragraphs, approved or rejected whole.

fragments.text: Each change is one page: a card with the page's title and type, "new page" or "edited", the number of paragraphs inserted and pins added (verified and not, in words), then the page shown with every inserted paragraph on a pale yellow background and the rest in grey, pins as chips. Two buttons, **Approve this page** and **Reject this page**, and a line "change 3 of 9". Nothing is written until Approve is pressed; a rejected page stays exactly as loaded and the rejection is noted in the log entry.
- **Approval.** Pages changed in the wiki equal approved cards; the log entry lists approved and rejected pages by slug; no page differs from its loaded body without an approved card naming it.

options.label: Per claim
options.description: One decision per inserted paragraph: you can keep three of a page's five insertions; the page is rebuilt from what you kept.

fragments.text: Each change is one inserted paragraph: a card names the page and the heading it goes under, shows the paragraph with its pins as chips, and has **Keep** and **Drop**; cards are grouped by page, "claim 7 of 31". The new source page is one card per section. When every card of a page is decided, the page is rebuilt from the kept paragraphs; a page with nothing kept is not changed; a heading left empty is dropped with its section. A page-level button **Keep every verified claim on this page** decides at once the cards whose pins all verified.

- **Approval.** Every paragraph in a changed page that was not in its loaded body corresponds to exactly one kept card; dropped cards appear nowhere; the log entry gives kept and dropped counts per page.

questions.question: What happens to a drafted claim whose quotation the code cannot find in the library passage?

options.label: Drop it
options.description: The claim leaves the proposal and is listed with the model's quote and the nearest passage, so nothing unverified can be filed.

fragments.text: A box **Could not verify: n** lists each failed quote with the passage the model named, the nearest passage on that page and an **Open the PDF page** button; these claims are in no change card and in no later prompt.

- **Failed takeaway** = `verify` false. It is kept in `failed[]` with the model's quote and the nearest passage (the passage on that page sharing the longest run of consecutive normalised words with the quote, and that run's length), and excluded from every later prompt.

- **Unverified.** After an ingest the count of ⚠ pins in the wiki is unchanged (0 in the file I looked at) and every pin in a changed page verifies; the "could not verify" count plus the verified takeaways equal the takeaways returned.

options.label: Keep as ⚠
options.description: The claim stays with the ⚠ mark and a note; Lint lists it until someone fixes or removes it.

fragments.text: A failed quote stays in its paragraph as a pin marked **⚠ not found on PDF page n**, with the nearest passage shown beside it; the change card counts "2 pins not verified" in amber and in words, and a page approved with a ⚠ pin is filed with `status` "draft". Lint lists every ⚠ pin with its page.

- **Failed takeaway** = `verify` false. The pin is built all the same with the model's quote and the mark ⚠; the nearest passage (the passage on that page sharing the longest run of consecutive normalised words with the quote) is kept for the chip.

- **Unverified.** After an ingest the number of ⚠ pins in the wiki equals the number of failed quotes kept in approved pages, Lint's "unverified pins" line shows the same number, and every approved page holding one has `status` "draft".

options.label: Retry once
options.description: The failed quotes go back to the model once with the passage texts, asking for the exact words; what still fails is dropped. One more call.

fragments.text: A box **Could not verify: n** lists each failed quote; a button **Ask the model for the exact words (1 call, n passages)** sends the failed claims with the full text of the passages they named and asks for a quotation copied verbatim. What verifies joins the takeaways; what still fails is listed in grey and left out of every change.

- **Failed takeaway** = `verify` false. On retry, each is re-sent once as `{claim, passage id, passage text}` with "copy 8 to 40 words exactly as they stand"; the answer is verified by the same rule; a second failure is final and excluded from every later prompt.

- **Unverified.** After an ingest the count of ⚠ pins in the wiki is unchanged (0 in the file I looked at); the panel shows failed before the retry, recovered by it and still failing, and the three add up.

questions.question: What leaves the browser when you ask the wiki a question?

options.label: Pages only
options.description: The index first, then up to five pages the model chose; the answer may only reuse pins that already stand on those pages.

fragments.text: Step 1 sends the index and the question; the model returns up to five slugs, shown as chips with a **Change pages** link that lets you tick others. Step 2 sends those pages' bodies, announced as "5 pages, 41,200 characters; 0 library passages have left the browser", and the question. The answer's pins must already stand on the pages sent; one that does not is shown struck through with "not on the pages sent".

- **Ask, call 1** = the index + the question → JSON `{pages: [slug…]}`, kept to slugs that exist, at most 5. **Call 2** = the bodies of the chosen pages + the question → JSON `{title, answer, cannot_answer}`, answer at most 350 words. A pin in the answer is accepted when the same `pin:id#pPAGE` with the same quote exists in a sent page's body and `verify` is true; otherwise it is struck through. Characters sent = the lengths of the strings sent, added up; passages sent = 0.

options.label: Pages and passages
options.description: The chosen pages and also the library passages they pin, up to 25, so the model can quote the source directly and add new pins; more leaves the browser.

fragments.text: Step 1 sends the index and the question; the model returns up to five slugs, shown as chips with a **Change pages** link. Step 2 sends those pages' bodies and the passages they pin, up to 25, announced as "5 pages, 41,200 characters, and 25 library passages have left the browser". The answer may pin any passage sent; every pin, old or new, is verified before it is shown, and a pin not already on the pages is marked "new, verified".

- **Ask, call 1** = the index + the question → JSON `{pages: [slug…]}`, kept to slugs that exist, at most 5. **Call 2** = the bodies of the chosen pages, the passages those pages pin ranked by how many pins point to each and cut at 25, as `{id, page, paragraph, text}`, and the question → JSON `{title, answer, cannot_answer}`, answer at most 350 words. Every pin in the answer runs through `verify`; a pin whose document and page are not among the passages or pages sent is struck through. Passages sent = the number of passage objects in the prompt.

questions.question: How should an answer treat the law and the commentary?

options.label: All, labelled
options.description: One answer; every pin carries the register letter of its document, and the prompt tells the model to name the register where it matters.

fragments.text: The answer comes as one text. Each pin chip carries its document's register letter and name ("(c) UN report"), and the prompt says: name the register where it matters, keep the document's own verb, never present (c) to (f) as what the treaty requires. Under the answer, one line counts the verified pins by register.
- **Register of a pin** = the register of its document (above), shown on every chip; the count line is one number per letter over the answer's verified pins.

options.label: Law first
options.description: The answer comes in two parts: what treaty text and General Comments say, then what reports, institutions, civil society and scholarship add.

fragments.text: The answer comes in two parts the prompt asks for: **What the law says** (pins to documents of register (a) or (b) only; "the library has no treaty-body view on this" when there is none) and **What the reports and commentary add** (registers (c) to (f)). The code checks the letters of each part's pins and moves a pin in the wrong part to a line "in the wrong part". Under the answer, one line counts the verified pins by register.

- **Register of a pin** = the register of its document (above). The answer JSON has `law` and `commentary` instead of `answer`; a pin in `law` whose letter is not a or b, or in `commentary` whose letter is a or b, is listed under "in the wrong part" and counted in neither.

plan_base:
# Research wiki workspace: neurotechnology in the administration of justice

## Context

A team of human rights professionals follows what ten documents say about neurotechnology in the justice system. The wiki in `WORKSHOP_DATA.wiki` is their compiled knowledge: 40 pages written by models, every claim pinned to a passage of `WORKSHOP_DATA.library` with a verbatim quote. What goes wrong today is upkeep and trust: a new report arrives and nobody reads it into the pages; a chatbot's answer cannot be checked; a report that quotes a General Comment gets cited as if it were one. This app is the workspace: read and navigate, ask the wiki and file good answers back, ingest the waiting document with a person approving each change, and lint. The model drafts; the code verifies every quotation; a person decides. Nothing is called on page load; every call to the model is announced with what leaves the browser.

## What I found in the data

Numbers are from the files I examined; the app computes its own at load.

- 40 pages: 9 source, 14 concept, 14 entity, 3 question; 39 `status` "reviewed", 1 "stub" (`a-hrc-57-61`, an entity page for the inbox document, 11 pins all to other documents, 16 pages linking to it, a ten-item list of what the ingest should check).
- 707 pins, all marked ✓, the number the index states. 625 quotes are whole; 82 join fragments of one passage with "…". A substring check fails those 82; the fragment rule below verifies all 707. Every label matches a passage on its page: "para. N" where the passage has `paragraph` (323 pins), "p. label" where it does not (384).
- Pins per document: A/81/351 227, AHRC-2025 146, UNODC-INTERPOL-2025 78, FuturesLab-2026 75, Szoszkiewicz-Yuste-2025 68, CCPR/C/GC/32 45, CCPR/C/21/Rev.1/Add.4 26, CCPR/C/GC/34 25, Prainsack-et-al-2022 17, A/HRC/57/61 0.
- Six `contested` blocks, one each on six concept pages; the tensions register has the same six cards and five discrepancies of fact. Verdicts: leans-contest 3, contested 2, leans-support 1.
- Links: no dangling `[[slug]]`, no orphan page, `frontmatter.sources` equals the set of pinned documents on every page; `frontmatter.links` and body links differ on 5 entries.
- Sizes: bodies 3,980 to 23,216 characters (median 8,210), 347,911 in all, about 87,000 tokens: no single call can carry the wiki. Index 6,990 characters, log 7,893, tensions 5,568, schema 12,446. Markdown used: headings to `###`, bold, italic, bullets, numbered lists, `[[slug]]`, pins, plain links, fenced `contested` blocks; no tables or images.
- Library: 10 documents; `symbol` null for 5; `paragraph` set in the five UN documents, null in the rest; `page_label` can be "3471" or "e773"; curly quotes in 120 passages, a hyphen followed by a space in 6.
- A/HRC/57/61: `status` "inbox", 100 passages on PDF pages 2–20 (the annex is left out), 61,737 characters, paragraphs 1–84, sub-paragraphs as their own passages ("78 (a)" to "80 (f)"); the passage "5 (a)" holds (b) and (c) inside its text; `section` is a broken fragment for two headings. 13 passages mention justice terms; 29 with evidence, torture and the recommendations.

## The app, screen by screen

1. **Header.** Title "Research wiki: neurotechnology in the administration of justice"; one line from the data: "`pages.length` pages (n sources, n concepts, n entities, n questions) · n pins, n verified by this page · `library.records.length` documents, n in the inbox · built `wiki.built`". A status strip: "Changes this session: n · Calls to the model: m · Passages that left the browser: k", the button **Download the wiki**, and the warning "This page has no storage: changes live in it until you download them."
2. **Sidebar (left, 320 px).** A filter box ("title, tag or slug"); the pages listed by type, each with its `title`, register letters and pin count computed by the code, stubs tagged "stub"; tabs **Pages**, **Log**, **Tensions**, **Lint**. Under the list: **Ask the wiki**, one **Ingest `symbol`** button per library document whose `status` is "inbox" (`short_title` when `symbol` is null; none when the inbox is empty), and **Lint now**.
3. **Page view (main column).** The `title`; badges for `type`, register letters with their names (a treaty law … f scholarship), `status`, `updated`; the `tags`. The `body` rendered: headings, bold, italic, lists, paragraphs; `[[slug]]` as a link to that page (a dangling one in red, "no page"); plain links in a new tab; pins as chips (item 4); `contested` blocks as cards (item 5). Below the body: **Links out** (`frontmatter.links`; those absent from the body marked "frontmatter only"), **Linked from** (every page whose body contains `[[this slug]]`) and **Sources** (`frontmatter.sources`, each with the document's `short_title`, `kind`, `year`, `url`, and "inbox" where it is not ingested). A button **Copy page as markdown** (frontmatter as YAML, then the body). Navigation through `location.hash = slug`, so back and forward work.
4. **Pin chips.** The label is a button; clicking it calls `studio.openSource(id, page)`. Beside it, the verification the code computed: "✓ verified" in green or "⚠ not found" in amber, in words as well as colour; where that differs from the mark written in the page, the chip adds "page says ✓" or "page says ⚠". An arrow expands the chip: the quote, the matching passage's `paragraph` or `page_label` and its first 300 characters, "Open the PDF page". The document's register letter is on the chip.
5. **Contested cards.** From each fenced block: the claim as heading; the verdict in words ("leans contest") first and large; the note; the lean bar labelled "descriptive: support n% of weighted positions, weights a 5 · b 4 · c 3 · d 2 · e 1 · f ½; the verdict is the answer"; then the positions as a table with a `caption` (sign in words, register, pin chip, gloss, page link). A link "in the tensions register" when a `###` entry there names this page in `card:`.
6. **Log and Tensions tabs.** The `log` rendered newest first (a toggle flips it), each `## [date] op | subject` collapsible; the `tensions` register with each `card:` link opening its page. Entries added in this session carry "this session".
7. **Ask the wiki.** A labelled text box, an "Ask the wiki" button, Enter sends; a grey box above states what each step will send before it goes. {{q4}} {{q5}} It is rendered like a page, inside `data-source="ai"`, every pin chip verified by the code, with "What the library cannot answer" from the model's `cannot_answer`. Under it: **File as a question page** (item 9), **Copy answer**, **Ask again**. Each step has a progress line and a Stop button; a parse failure shows the raw answer with "Retry".
8. **Ingest.** A stepper with four steps and one running line: "calls so far m · passages sent k". **Step 1, scope.** {{q1}} **Step 2, takeaways.** As each batch returns, a table grows: claim, quote, passage (paragraph and PDF page), the pages it would touch (slugs as chips), and the verification result in words. {{q3}} **Step 3, drafts.** "Draft the source page (1 call)" sends the verified takeaways; the draft appears as a change card. Then "Draft the changes to n pages (n calls)" runs one call per touched page with a progress line and Stop; the stub `a-hrc-57-61` is always among them, rewritten with its ten-item checklist sent along. **Step 4, review and file** (item 10).
9. **Filing a question page.** A card previews the page the code builds: slug from the title (kebab-case, unique), `type` "question", `tags` typed by the user, `register` from the pinned documents, `status` "draft", `updated` today, `links` from the `[[slugs]]` in the answer, `sources` from the pins; body = "# title", "**Short answer.**", "## Reasoning" (the answer), "## What the library cannot answer", "## Related". **File this page** adds it to `pages`, its line to the index under Questions and `## [date] ask | title` to the log. Disabled, with the reason, until every pin in the answer verifies.
10. **Change review.** {{q2}} After the last decision, **File the approved changes** writes them at once: pages replaced or added with `updated` today; the index updated (item "Index line" below); `## [date] ingest | symbol: short_title` appended to the log; any new contested card added to the tensions register; the document's `status` set to "ingested" in memory; Lint re-run. Until then nothing in the wiki changes.
11. **Lint tab.** A table of checks, each with its count and the pages concerned as links: dangling links; orphans; pins not verified by the code; pins marked ✓ that fail; `sources` that differ from the documents pinned; pages with no pins; `links` not reciprocated; pages missing from the index or index lines without a page; index ✓N that differs from the computed count; contested cards without a tensions entry and the reverse; stub pages; pins to a document still in the inbox. Each reads "0 · pass" or "n · check"; a **Re-run** button. The schema's reading for contradictions is named on screen as not done by code.
12. **Checks panel** (below the header, open by default), **Download**, and a **footer** with `wiki.source`, `wiki.built` and "Counting, matching and verification are done by this page's code; the model is called only when you press Ask, Ingest or a retry button."

## How every number is computed

- **Load.** `P = WORKSHOP_DATA.wiki.pages`, `D = WORKSHOP_DATA.library.records`, maps slug → page and id → document. Per page: `bodyLinks` = the slugs in `/\[\[([^\]|#]+)/g`; `pins` = every match of `/\[([^\]]+)\]\(pin:([^#\s)]+)#p(\d+)(?: "([^"]*)")?\) ?(✓|⚠)/g` (label, id, page, quote, mark); `backlinks[slug]` = pages whose `bodyLinks` contain it. Header counts are `P.length`, counts by `type`, pins and verified pins summed, documents with `status` "inbox".
- **Normalise** `norm(s)`: Unicode NFKC; “ ” „ → "; ‘ ’ → '; en and em dash → "-"; soft hyphen removed; a hyphen followed by whitespace → "" ("decision- making" = "decision-making"); runs of whitespace → one space; trimmed. Capitals are kept (the schema says words and capitals must match).
- **verify(pin)** = true when a passage `x` of document `id` with `x.page === page` exists such that the quote, split on "…" or "..." into fragments, has every fragment found in `norm(x.text)` in order, each search starting where the previous fragment ended; and the label contains "para. " + `x.paragraph` when `x.paragraph` is set, otherwise "p. " + `x.page_label`. A pin with no quote, an unknown `id`, or a document whose `status` is "inbox" is not verified, with the reason kept for the chip. The 707 pins of the file I examined all verify by this rule.
- **Cite-as** for a document = the most frequent text before ", para." or ", p." in the existing pins' labels to it; with no pins, its `symbol`, or `author` + " " + `year` when `symbol` is null. **New pin** = `[cite-as, para. <paragraph>](pin:id#p<page> "quote") ✓` (", p. <page_label>" when `paragraph` is null); straight double quotes inside the quote become “ ” first, so the regular expression still matches.
- **Register of a document** = the `register` of the source page whose `sources` is exactly [that id], else of the stub page with that `sources`, else "?". A new page's `register` = the registers of its pinned documents.
- **Contested card** from a block: `claim`, `verdict`, `note` by prefix; a position line splits on " | " into sign, register, pin, gloss, page. **Lean** = (Σ weight of "+" + ½ Σ weight of "~") ÷ Σ weight of all positions, weights a 5, b 4, c 3, d 2, e 1, f 0.5, shown as a percentage with the formula.
- **Calls to the model.** One function for every call: it shows the prompt's size in characters and the passage objects in it, adds both to the session counters, calls `await studio.ask(prompt, {json: true})`, parses JSON (once more after stripping a fenced code block), and on failure shows the raw answer with Retry. Every prompt states the pin syntax and "quote only words that stand in the passages given; the code will check".

- **Takeaway call** (one per batch): the batch's passages as `{id, page, paragraph, text}`, the index, and "return JSON {takeaways: [{claim, quote, passage, pages}]}, at most 10, quote 8 to 40 words copied verbatim from that one passage, pages = slugs from the index the claim bears on". For each takeaway the code finds the passage by `id`, builds the pin and runs `verify`; `pages` are kept to slugs that exist, plus at most two new slugs per ingest, which become "new page" cards.

- **Source page call**: the verified takeaways with their ready-made pins, the cite-as, the document's `title`, `author`, `published`, `pages` and `url`, the schema's source-page anatomy (Full cite, Register, One-liner, Key takeaways, How NOT to read this, Where it feeds the wiki, Related) and "return JSON {one_liner, body, touches: [{slug, why}]}, body at most 900 words, only the pins given, copied exactly". The code re-verifies every pin in `body`, builds the frontmatter itself (`type` "source", `register` from the stub, `sources` [id], `links` from the body, `tags` from the touched slugs) and keeps `touches` to existing or allowed new slugs, at most 12, the stub added if missing.
- **Touched page call** (one per slug): the page's `body`, the takeaways whose `pages` include the slug, with their pins, and "return JSON {edits: [{after, markdown}], contested}, each `after` an existing heading or 'end', at most 300 words in all, pins copied exactly, `contested` a full block only where this document disagrees with the page". The code inserts each `markdown` at the end of the named heading's section (at the end of the page, with a note, when the heading is not found), re-verifies every pin, adds the link both ways in `links` and the document id to `sources`.
- **Index line** = "- [[slug]] — one-liner · (letters) · ✓N", N the verified pins counted by the code; the source page's line goes under Sources, the stub's is replaced, touched pages' N recomputed, the first line rebuilt from the counts. **Log entry**: "Read n passages (cite-as, register (x)). Wrote [[slug]]. N pins in all; besides its own page, pinned on k pages: [[…]]. Rejected: [[…]]." **Tensions entry** for a new card: `### slug-of-claim`, `title`, `status` (contested → open; leans-* → leaning; settled-* → settled), `card: [[page]]`, `poles` and `where` from the positions.
- **Download** = a Blob of JSON in the shape of `WORKSHOP_DATA.wiki` (pages, index, log, tensions, schema, count) plus `changes` (each approved change with date and kind) and `library_status`, saved as `wiki-<date>.json` through a temporary `<a download>`; a second button saves the changed pages as one markdown file with `---` separators.

## How the app checks itself

A panel of one-line checks: what was compared, the values, "pass" in green or "check" in red, with the pages concerned as links. A failing check never hides a page or a pin.

- **Pins.** Pins found by the regular expression against the number stated in the first line of the index (`/(\d[\d,]*) pins/`); verified against found; any ✓ that fails listed with its page.
- **Labels.** Every verified pin's label matches its passage's `paragraph` or `page_label`.
- **Structure.** Dangling links 0; orphans 0; `sources` equal pinned documents on every page; every page in the index and every index `[[slug]]` a page; contested cards equal tensions `card:` entries.
- **Model answers.** For every call: JSON parsed; slugs that do not exist listed; takeaways returned, verified and failed adding up.

- **Filing.** After filing: the new or changed pages re-parsed and re-verified; the index line count equals the page's verified pins; the log's last entry names the pages changed; Lint re-run and its before and after counts shown side by side.
- **Session.** Changes listed equal the log entries added this session; the download's page count equals `pages.length`.

## Edge cases and risks

- The model may change a quote while "copying" it: every pin is re-verified after every call, never trusted from the mark it wrote. A straight `"` inside a quote would break the pin syntax: the code makes it curly first.
- A sub-paragraph passage ("5 (a)") carries (b) and (c) in its text: the label is the passage's `paragraph` as stored, and the chip shows the passage so a reader sees where the words sit. `section` is broken for two headings of A/HRC/57/61: shown as stored, never used as a heading in a draft.
- Footnotes, tables and captions are not in the passages: a pin cannot verify them; the chip says so.
- A model answer may name a slug that does not exist (dropped and listed) or propose a new page with an existing slug (treated as an edit of that page).
- `studio.ask` can fail or return prose: the raw answer is shown, nothing is filed, Retry re-sends the same prompt; Stop keeps what has returned.
- Everything lives in memory: reloading loses the session, so the warning line stays visible and Download sits in the header. The counters show calls and passages before and after each step; a whole ingest of the inbox document is at most about 4 + 1 + 12 calls.
- The lean bar can mislead: the verdict comes first and the bar is labelled descriptive, as the schema requires. Registers are on every chip so a (c) report is never read as (b).

## Design and accessibility

- Two columns at 1,280 px (sidebar 320 px, text column up to 900 px), one column below 900 px; system font stack at 16 px; one accent colour (#1f6fb2); verified and not, pass and fail, in words as well as colour; inserted text on a pale yellow background with a left border.
- From "The A11Y Project checklist": a visible focus style on every button, link and chip; button labels unique and descriptive ("Approve change 3 of 9", "Open A/HRC/57/61 at PDF page 12"); every input has a `<label>`; change cards are a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`; every table has a `<caption>`; text contrast 4.5:1, chips and borders 3:1.
- From the quality-assurance guidance on generative AI (UK Government Analysis Function): nothing a model wrote enters the wiki before a person has read it, and the prompt box says what leaves the browser before it leaves.
- From Karpathy's "LLM Wiki" and the author's schema: the library is read-only; the index is read before pages; the log is append-only; the three operations are the three buttons.
- Keyboard: the filter box has focus on load; `aria-live="polite"` on progress lines, counters and the "Filed" message; Escape stops a running step; nothing opens in a modal. Every model output sits inside `data-source="ai"`; every computed value has a "How this is computed" note.

## Out of scope

No free-text editing of pages by hand. No PDF viewer inside the app (`studio.openSource` does that). No search beyond the sidebar filter. No version history beyond this session's change list. No lint of contradictions by the model. No ingest of a document that is not in the inbox, and no second ingest of the same document. No export other than JSON and markdown.
